scenes.name: Motown: Supremes y Holland-Dozier-Holland
scenes.author: Jon Savage
scenes.desc: Los grupos de Tamla/Motown ocuparon el hueco de los girl groups: Martha and the Vandellas («Heat Wave», «Dancing in the Street», «Nowhere to Run»), Gladys Knight, las Marvelettes, las Velvelettes y, sobre todo, las Supremes, el grupo pop americano de más éxito del momento (seis números 1 en dos años). Tres amigas del proyecto Brewster-Douglass, las «Supremes sin éxitos» hasta «Where Did Our Love Go» (1964): Berry Gordy vio en ellas el caballo de Troya para entrar en el mercado blanco, con los Funk Brothers, la escritura «psicológica» de Holland-Dozier-Holland (playlets femeninos sobre el amor como adicción, música dura contra letras sumisas) y el departamento de Artist Development de Maxine Powell y Cholly Atkins. Su imagen de espectáculo (Copacabana, pelucas) contrastaba con la nueva bohemia rock, como en su incómodo encuentro con unos Beatles fumados. Diana Ross ardía: seis números 1 y aún las trataban como a un grupo cualquiera.

podcast.title: Attempted Bowie Bonds
podcast.body: This songwriting team attempted to create financial instruments similar to Bowie Bonds, securitizing their music royalties to generate capital. "James Brown, the songwriting team of Holland Dozier Holland, the Isle of Brothers, Ashford and Simpson, even the guy who wrote songs like I Love Rock and Roll for Joan Jett, and another songwriter who wrote songs for Rod Stewart and Tupac."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Autobiography Title
podcast.body: The autobiography of Brian and Eddie Holland is named after "Come and Get These Memories," despite the team having co-written many bigger and more obvious hits. This highlights the significance of that song as the beginning of the Motown sound. "Brian and Eddie Holland's autobiography is named after this, rather than after any of the bigger and more obvious hits they would like to co-write."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs
srcs.episode: Episode 111: "Heat Wave" by Martha and the Vandellas

podcast.title: Division of Labor
podcast.body: Within the Holland, Dozier and Holland team, Brian Holland and Lamont Dozier typically took charge of the musical aspects, including riffs, hooks, melodies, chord changes, and studio work with drummers, keyboardists, and bass players. Eddie Holland primarily concentrated on crafting lyrics, focusing on meaning and "repeat formation." "Holland Dozier and Holland, really Brian Holland and the Montdozier, who took charge of the musical side of things with Eddie concentrating on the lyrics, would make their own."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs
srcs.episode: Episode 111: "Heat Wave" by Martha and the Vandellas

podcast.title: Followed Bowie Bonds Model
podcast.body: The Motown songwriting team of Holland-Dozier-Holland followed David Bowie's innovative financial model, utilizing intellectual property to secure financial instruments after the success of the Bowie Bonds. This demonstrated the broader impact of Bowie's pioneering business acumen in the music industry. "And once the Bowie bonds sold, others followed, including the Motown songwriting team of Holland-Doseyour Holland, as well as a number of other professional songwriters."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Lamont Dozier's Death
podcast.body: Lamont Dozier, who was one-third of the highly influential Motown songwriting team Holland-Dozier-Holland, died on August 8th at the age of 81. "That very same day at Lamont Dozier, one-third of the great Motown songwriting team, Holland Dozier Holland, died at the age of 81."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: In Memoriam of Those Lost in 2022

podcast.title: Motown Domination
podcast.body: The team of Holland, Dozier and Holland were pivotal in Motown's domination of the American charts throughout the rest of the decade, following the release of their defining "Motown sound" record for Martha and the Van Dellers. They transitioned from minor players to the most important team for the label's commercial success. "it began a domination of the American charts that would last the rest of the decade, a domination caused in large part by the team of Holland, Dozier and Holland."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs

xref.title: Attempted Bowie Bonds
xref.body: James Brown was one of several artists who attempted to replicate David Bowie's financial innovation, the Bowie Bonds, by securitizing his own music royalties. "Other artists tried the same thing. James Brown, the songwriting team of Holland Dozier Holland, the Isle of Brothers, Ashford and Simpson, even the guy who wrote songs like I Love Rock and Roll for Joan Jett, and another songwriter who wrote songs for Rod Stewart and Tupac."
